jobs.occupation: Tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor Functional Biology and Ecology of Marine Animals
jobs.description:
Department of Biology, Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen, Denmark

  The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as Tenure-track or Associate Professor in functional biology and ecology of marine animals. The position is set to be filled by June 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, pending negotiation.

  Position Overview
 We are looking for a passionate, innovative and collaborative researcher with expertise in hypothesis driven research on the functional biology and experimental ecology of marine animals. The ideal candidate will complement and strengthen our existing research areas, and take advantage of our experimental facilities and easy access to different coastal ecosystems. We expect the successful candidate to take a leading role in establishing an externally funded research program and take an active part in developing existing and new courses in the teaching curriculum of the section.

  Key responsibilities include:

   	
• Leading research initiatives and securing third-party funding 	
• Teaching and supervising students at undergraduate, graduate, and PhD levels, with primary teaching responsibilities in the biology degree program 	
• Disseminating research and scientific results to the public 	
• Participating in departmental committees and other tasks as requested   The Research Environment
 The candidate will join the Section for Marine Biology, which operates across both the Copenhagen and Helsingør campuses. The position will be based in Helsingør, where laboratory and office facilities will be provided. The section’s research encompasses a wide range of topics within marine biology including aquatic microbiology and virology, sensory biology, physiology and functional biology of marine organisms, climate change biology, aquaculture, coral reef biology, deep sea biology and the diversity, phylogeny, and evolution of metazoans and protists. Studies are conducted across polar, temperate, and (sub)tropical ecosystems.

  The section boasts modern laboratories equipped with state-of-the-art tools and infrastructure for experimental research including sea-water facilities for animal keeping. This also includes specialized labs for microenvironmental analyses, respirometry, electrophysiology, advanced bioimaging, and DNA and RNA analyses. Additionally, our research vessel, Ophelia, and the proximity to diverse marine habitats in Øresund and other areas provide an excellent platform for a broad range of biological studies.

  We encourage interdisciplinary collaborations within the department and externally with industry and public research institutions, where synergistic benefits are evident.

  Qualifications and Profile
 Applicants should have a strong background in functional biology and experimental ecology of marine animals and their response to environmental changes. Applicants must demonstrate a proven ability to conduct independent, original, and hypothesis-driven experimental research at an international level. 

  Applicants should be capable of teaching a variety of topics within animal science and ecology in the BSc and MSc biology programs and are expected to contribute by developing new courses.

  Qualifications for Tenure-track Assistant Professor level: 

   	
• A strong publication trajectory in high-level, international, peer-reviewed ISI journals 	
• Experience with personal research grants or participation (by name) in major grants 	
• Research plans and publication records that demonstrate clear potential for attracting external funding 	
• Academic standing reflecting internationally competitive research and/or high potential to make a future scientific impact at the international level 	
• Documented university-level teaching experience is advantageous but not mandatory 	
• If not already holding formal pedagogical qualifications, the candidate must complete pedagogical training equivalent to the University of Copenhagen’s Teaching and Learning in Higher Education Program for Assistant Professors   Qualifications for Associate Professor level: 

   	
• A substantial publication record in high-level, international, peer-reviewed ISI journals 	
• A proven track record of securing major external research funding 	
• Documented university-level experience in delivering high-quality undergraduate/graduate teaching, with the ability to explain and reflect on own teaching practices 	
• Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen’s teacher training program 	
• Managerial and outreach experience   The Department of Biology (BIO) employs around 425 academic and technical staff and hosts research programs and teaching curricula that cover all major biological sub-disciplines. University rankings typically place the field of biology and biochemistry at the University of Copenhagen first in Denmark and among the top 15-25 universities globally. We offer PhD, BSc, and MSc programs in biology, biochemistry, molecular biomedicine, and bioinformatics, engaging around 1,800 students.

  The department is committed to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment that reflects the diversity of society. At BIO, we see diversity as a strength. We highly value a safe and collaborative working atmosphere, and offer a friendly and thriving international research environment with opportunities to build internationally competitive research groups. Excellent opportunities are available for research funding to establish oneself in Denmark.

  Learn out more about working at BIO here.

  Copenhagen is among the 10 most livable cities in the world with a vibrant music, dance and theater culture, world class restaurants, an extensive public transportation system and excellent opportunities for biking in the city. Life for families is made easy by a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual career opportunities, maternity/paternity leave and six weeks of annual vacation.

  Assessment of applicants 
 Assessment of applicants for the tenure-track assistant professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

  Assessment of applicants for the associate professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  University of Copenhagen’s criteria for recognising merit
 General criteria apply to the appointment of assistant professor / associate professor at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here:
 
 For tenure-track assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf

  For associate professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5b_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Associate_professors.pdf

  Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  The Appointment Committee will prepare a short-list of applicants at both levels to be assessed by an Assessment Committee. Note that being on the short-list, is not equivalent to being assessed qualified for the position. Short-listed candidate may potentially be deemed “not qualified” by the Assessment Committee. 

  A sub-set of the qualified short-listed candidates will be selected for a formal interview by the Appointment Committee.  Invited candidates may also be given the opportunity to visit the department to meet with the faculty and the Head of Department, and to give a research presentation.

  Terms of employment
 The position is open from June 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is either as tenure-track assistant professor or associate professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  We encourage women and members of other underrepresented groups to apply, as we are committed to diversifying our department and fostering an inclusive environment.

  Information on tenure-track program
 An assigned mentor will provide the tenure-track assistant professor with guidance related to career development, other academic topics, and administrative procedures.

  Performance of the tenure-track assistant professor will be followed via internal yearly evaluations and a mid-term and final international evaluation by an assessment committee. If the ‘final appraisal’ is positive you will be promoted to associate professor. Performance and progression towards the criteria above will be evaluated with due consideration of differences between research fields.

  Further information
 For more information about the Department of Biology and the various research sections, please visit our website https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/.

  Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department, Professor Edda Klipp (Head-of-Department@bio.ku.dk) or Head of Section, Associate Professor Anders Garm (algarm@bio.ku.dk). 

  International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. Useful information is also available at The International Staff Mobility office (ISM) at the University of Copenhagen (https://ism.ku.dk). ISM offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

  Filing of application
 The position may be applied for at the tenure-track assistant professor and Associate Professor level. Please note that it is possible to apply at more than one level. If applied at more than one level, separate applications must be submitted (see below).

  The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarships in Quantum Physics: Quantum Opto-Acoustics, Optomechanics, Microscopy and Computing - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Can a massive crystal be placed in a quantum superposition? Can squeezed light control the motion of a membrane? Can we see structures that conventional microscopes miss – and make fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing possible with today’s imperfect quantum states?

At DTU Physics, we are recruiting four PhD students to explore these challenges through three experimental projects and one theory-and-software project. The positions are based in the Section for Quantum Physics and Information Technology (QPIT) and bigQ – Center for Macroscopic Quantum States. You will join an international research environment combining advanced quantum-optical laboratories, quantum information theory and large-scale computational research.

The PhD projects
Each position addresses a different frontier in quantum science. You may apply for one or several projects; please indicate your preferences and explain how your background matches the chosen research direction(s).

Quantum Control of Macroscopic Mechanical Motion (Quantum Opto-Acoustics): How far can quantum mechanics be pushed toward the macroscopic world? Our experiment uses cavity-enhanced Brillouin interactions to control a 12 GHz acoustic mode in a millimeter-sized quartz crystal with an effective mass of 170 micrograms, already cooled extremely close to its quantum ground state. You will develop quantum-control and optical readout techniques to create non-classical mechanical states, including single-phonon excitations and Schrödinger-cat superpositions. You will also explore optical–acoustic entanglement and quantum memories, aiming to turn a massive crystal into a resource for quantum information and fundamental tests of quantum physics.

Quantum-Enhanced Optomechanics with Ultracoherent Membranes: Can we transfer the quantum properties of light to a vibrating membrane? This project builds on our density-phononic-crystal membrane in a high-finesse optical cavity, combining a mechanical quality factor above 100 million with exceptionally strong optomechanical interactions at room temperature. You will develop quantum-limited measurements, suppress technical noise, and implement optical cooling and feedback to approach the mechanical ground state. A central ambition is to interface the membrane with squeezed light, enabling mechanical squeezing, light–mechanics entanglement, and ultimately coherent quantum-state transfer.

Quantum-Enhanced Microscopy through Spatial-Mode Engineering: Can we distinguish microscopic objects that conventional microscopes cannot resolve? This project explores spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE), a technique for extracting spatial information inaccessible to conventional intensity imaging. You will develop advanced optical measurements to improve nanoparticle detection and localization using Rayleigh scattering microscopy, and extend these methods to chemically selective Raman microscopy. By combining spatial-mode engineering, quantum estimation theory, and squeezed light, you will pursue improved imaging sensitivity and resolution, with applications in nanoscale sensing, chemical analysis, and biomedical diagnostics.

Fault-Tolerant Continuous-Variable Quantum Computing with GKP States: How much squeezing does a practical fault-tolerant optical quantum computer really need? This theory-and-software project aims to develop architectures for continuous-variable quantum computing based on Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill (GKP) states, targeting reliable computation below established squeezing thresholds. You will investigate improved GKP decoding, dual-level quantum error correction, optimized logical codes, and simplified measurement-based circuits. Using large-scale simulations and Danish high-performance computing infrastructure, you will develop open benchmarking software and evaluate realistic noise models and logical workloads, establishing a practical roadmap toward scalable photonic quantum computing.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will take ownership of a clearly defined research challenge while working closely with experienced researchers and technical staff. The experimental projects emphasize building and controlling quantum-optical setups; the computing project emphasizes theory, simulation, decoder development and reproducible software. Depending on your project, your responsibilities will include:

• Developing and optimizing optical cavities, precision measurements and low-noise control systems, or designing quantum algorithms, codes and simulation software.
• Formulating theoretical models and testing them through carefully designed experiments or realistic, large-scale numerical simulations.
• Quantifying noise, errors and performance limits; analysing results and developing robust data-analysis or benchmarking tools.
• Publishing scientific results, presenting at international conferences and collaborating with students, researchers, engineers and international partners.
We seek curious and motivated candidates with backgrounds in physics, quantum optics, photonics, optomechanics, mathematics, computer science, quantum information or related fields. For the experimental tracks, hands-on optical-laboratory skills, electronics and experimental programming are valuable. For the GKP computing track, strong analytical skills and experience with numerical simulation, quantum error correction or scientific software development are especially relevant. Across all four projects, we value creativity, rigorous thinking, initiative, persistence and constructive teamwork.

As a formal qualification, you must hold a two-year master’s degree (120 ECTS points), or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master’s degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship concerning translational tissue engineering for urethral reconstructions
jobs.description:
The Department of Pediatric Surgery at Julianne Marie Center, Rigshospitalet, is offering a three-year PhD fellowship. The PhD fellowship is within the field of pediatric surgery and tissue engineering and is available from December 1, 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. The Novo Nordisk Tandem Programme finances this PhD fellowship.

Aim of the PhD project

To conduct preclinical in vitro and in vivo studies to develop and evaluate perioperative layered autologous tissue expansion grafts for male urethral reconstruction.

Project description

Highly specialized centres in Paediatric Surgery and Urology treat children with a wide range of congenital malformations affecting the urinary and genital systems. Conditions such as bladder exstrophy, cloacal exstrophy, severe hypospadias, posterior urethral valves, and spina bifida may significantly affect the development and function of the urinary bladder and urethra. In most cases, surgical reconstruction can successfully restore anatomy and function. However, in more complex cases, tissue deficiency, poor tissue quality, and impaired innervation can pose major challenges to surgical reconstruction. These complications may result in substantial morbidity and, in some cases, even threaten the child's life. Long-term consequences can include impaired organ function, recurrent illness, dependence on medication, repeated surgical interventions, and lifelong medical care.

Reconstruction of tubular structures is particularly important in congenital urinary tract malformations. Examples include creating catheterizable channels to facilitate bladder emptying, reconstructing the penile urethra, and replacing or reconstructing the ureter to ensure adequate urine drainage from the kidney to the bladder. The overall aim of this project is to develop novel regenerative medicine approaches for reconstructive surgery in children with severe congenital malformations, with the ultimate goal of reducing morbidity and improving long-term quality of life. Specifically, the PhD project will focus on developing autologous tissue-engineered grafts for urethral reconstruction.

The scientific novelty lies in exploiting the body's own capacity for tissue regeneration by using the body as a bioreactor. This approach, referred to as guided tissue engineering, enables the development of autologous grafts in vivo, without the need for complex ex vivo cell expansion or specialized cell culture facilities. The method has the potential to be simple, cost-effective, and readily transferable to standard surgical settings, thereby making regenerative treatment accessible to a broader patient population. If successful, the approach could pave the way for clinical implementation, initially targeting patients with severe hypospadias who require complex urethral reconstruction.

Beyond paediatric reconstructive surgery, the findings may also have broader applications in other patient populations requiring tissue reconstruction, including adults undergoing reconstructive surgery following cancer treatment or severe trauma.

The PhD programme will comprise both in vitro studies and in vivo animal experiments to investigate and evaluate tissue-engineered constructs incorporating biomaterials and autologous tissues, with particular emphasis on their regenerative potential and suitability for reconstructive surgery.

Professor Magdalena Fossum, Department of Pediatric Surgery, Center for Cancer and Organ Diseases, Copenhagen University Hospital Rigshospitalet, Blegdamsvej 9, 2100 Copenhagen

Required qualifications

Are you passionate about finding technology solutions for drug development, so our scientists can focus on the science?

Do you have experience with IT product discovery and continuous development?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new IT Product Owner for the Scientific Solutions team.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

Our context

This position is based in our Global IT organization. Over the past five years, we have built and matured a product-driven organization with a strong focus on product management and lifecycle thinking. Our long-lived teams take ownership from problem discovery through solution delivery and continuous improvement, ensuring that we address real business needs.

Our structure combines clear leadership intent with empowered teams. Each team member is supported by a People Leader focused on development and a Functional Leader guiding strategy and delivery. We foster autonomy and self-organization to enable fast flow, clear accountability, and minimal dependencies.

The Scientific Solutions team supports Product Innovation, Product Development, CMC, Nonclinical Development, and Global Medical business functions. Across these areas, the common objective is to identify and develop technology solutions that enable pharmaceutical product innovation.

We are seeking a passionate IT Product Owner to join our growing Scientific Solutions team. As a key member of Global IT, you will play a crucial role in shaping coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data for a broad scientific user group.

This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment and collaborate with cross-functional, global teams to achieve extraordinary results.

You will report to Jakob Monajemzadeh Thrane, People Leader in Global IT, and, from a functional perspective to Ivanna Rosendal, Global Head of Digitalization. The position is based at our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Ensure that a broad scientific user group has coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data that evolve with their needs.

• Communicate closely and frequently with users and leadership teams to create a clear, shared understanding of the most important needs and priorities.

• Translate business needs into technology deliverables and coordinate with relevant IT teams to ensure prioritization and completion.

• Prioritize and manage the Scientific Solutions team’s backlog and actively help remove impediments to technology delivery.

• Collaborate closely with other teams across Global IT to manage dependencies and align priorities.

Qualifications and skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree, at minimum a master’s degree, and have 5+ years of experience in a related role within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or comparable scientific environment.

Furthermore, you have:

• A background that enables you to understand the translational stage of drug development.

• Hands-on experience managing and developing a technology product portfolio.

• Experience with product discovery and decision facilitation.

• Experience driving the successful delivery of digital products and platforms.

• Experience working in an agile team and continuously improving ways of working.

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, innovative and curious, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to be a proactive self-starter who can identify opportunities for improvement and take initiative to move things forward.

Our team needs to scale to support the ever-growing demands, so we need team members who both can act pragmatically, and solution orientated for the short term, and at the same time are able to think long-term to ensure what we do today can grow to support us in the future.

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

About Pandektes

Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

The experience you’ll bring

You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

What we offer

You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

We welcome candidates with interdisciplinary research backgrounds who can help realize our vision of creating lasting impact by guiding the shift toward a resilient and sustainable industry, society, and planet.

For this open position, we are seeking candidates to advance research in resilient and sustainable design of products and manufacturing solutions.

We prefer candidates that can demonstrate the potential for industrial application of their research. The candidate should bridge existing fields in the section and department, and we encourage applicants to address potential synergies in our educational programs and research activities.

The selected candidate will be required to teach relevant courses in the MPE educational program at the B.Sc., M.Sc., and PhD levels of the Mechanical and Production Engineering programs. 

Expected start date 
July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:

The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

For more information about the position contact Deputy Head of Department for Research Charles Møller (charles@mpe.au.dk / +45 61677786) or Head of Section Ramin Aghababaei ( ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 93508956)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than January 4th 2027.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. Shortlisting is used. Formalities and salary range

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.
